subject: Optional Steam game-server identity in independent game activity
scope: Read-only local source, cached official documentation and existing original-server IL. Research stopped for the user's shutdown request; no new connection, query, presence update or experiment was performed.
conclusion: The independent activity payload omits an optional server-identity field which steam-user can transport. Its relevance to Facepunch trusted counts is an unverified hypothesis, not a diagnosed cause or a verified fix.

facts: RustSession.steamGameActivity returns game_id 252490 while the run owns its transport/ticket lifecycle.
Once transportConnected is true, it adds the actual configured IPv4 address and game port.
It does not set steam_id_gs, is_secure, token, process_id or process_id_list.
applyIdle passes the activity object to client.gamesPlayed and retains the normal lifecycle cleanup behavior.
established.limit: Transport connection alone is not server authentication, game admission, EAC attestation, or trusted-count inclusion.

facts: The same message separately defines game_id, game_port, game_ip_address, is_secure and process-related fields.
Field presence in a protobuf schema does not establish when a game must set it or how a backend uses it.
Any future real server ID must remain an exact decimal string or equivalent uint64 representation, rather than being rounded through a JavaScript Number.
gamesPlayed normalizes numeric/string app entries, normalizes numeric game_ip_address to an IPv4 object, and passes existing object properties to ClientGamesPlayedWithDataBlob.
This function does not derive steam_id_gs from the current game IP/port or from ticket-validation events.
established.limit: This is an implementation capability, not evidence that supplying the field affects trusted counts.

schema.serializerEvidence: IL_0081 reads steamid; IL_0086 skips zero; IL_0089 writes tag 48; IL_0097 calls WriteUInt64.

facts: The inspected original producer obtains a pooled Approval and assigns world, hostname, official, encryption, version, nexus and DNS-endpoint fields before serialization.
It does not assign Approval.steamid, Approval.ipaddress or Approval.port.
A bounded full scan of this original Assembly-CSharp found no operand referring to Approval.steamid.

established.worker: approval_encryption currently reads only field 12 and skips other protobuf fields.
established.limit: A legacy schema field is not proof that the current target sends a nonzero server ID. No approval packet was newly decoded in this follow-up, and the remote server binary/configuration is not established by the local original assembly.

facts: A2S_INFO extra-data flag 0x10 carries a little-endian uint64 server SteamID.
The existing parser preserves that value as a decimal string under serverSteamId.
The published game-port field and the exact queried endpoint must be checked alongside the identity; an identity from a different server or an old restart must not be reused.
established.limit: No fresh A2S request was made. A public query reply alone does not establish the remote identity cryptographically or prove a particular account has authenticated to it.

facts: ClientTicketAuthComplete is matched to a cached ticket by its CRC; the implementation updates the cached estate and emits authTicketStatus for an own ticket.

The event exposes the reported validator SteamID. The installed source comment identifies this as the entity that validated an own ticket; the independent SteamKit evidence previously saved identifies the corresponding callback SteamID as the game server's SteamID.
The examined completion handler does not itself call gamesPlayed or fill its steam_id_gs field.
Current application diagnostics retain only active/validation booleans, so they do not establish a stored exact validator-to-current-run association.
established.limit: Any later use must bind a successful completion to the unique current lease, app, generation and destination, and reject cancellation/error/stale callbacks. A generic validated boolean is insufficient.

facts: The cached official page describes AdvertiseGame as rich presence for an unsecured game server.
For its steamIDGameServer parameter, that page specifies k_steamIDNonSteamGS when setting IP/port and k_steamIDNil when clearing it.
It states: When you are using Steam authentication system this call is never required, the auth system automatically sets the appropriate rich presence.
established.limit: This native SDK statement neither documents the internal CM mapping nor proves that a custom steam-user client reproduces every native association. It also does not require manually putting a real game-server ID into GamePlayed.steam_id_gs.

unverifiedHypothesis.statement: An independent custom Steam session might authenticate its ticket successfully while its explicit ClientGamesPlayed activity lacks the same current server association that the native Steam client maintains.
unverifiedHypothesis.support: The optional wire field exists, the application omits it, and the examined custom library paths do not populate it from authentication completion.
missingEvidence: A normal Rust client's actual CM activity field presence and server identity for the same target and version.
A normative requirement tying this field to authenticated server presence or Facepunch trusted counts.
A current exact server identity tied to the current independent ticket/run, rather than just an old public listing.
A controlled single-account result demonstrating changed trusted-count contribution independently of other sessions and batch timing.
notEstablished: That current independent authentication is missing or invalid.
That omitting steam_id_gs causes the observed count exclusion.
That adding the field would produce a protected EAC session or repair the server browser count.

nextSession: Confirm all temporary experiments and sessions were restored/stopped according to the main handoff before starting further work.
First obtain read-only evidence of a real validator/server identity tied to the current run and compare it privately with an exact-target current A2S identity; keep actual values out of reports.
Resolve or observe the normal client association path before deciding whether an implementation change is justified.
Any later experiment may report only the actual connected server's verified published identity and real address. Do not fabricate IDs, security flags, process identity or backend telemetry.
Treat any prospective field change as an unverified experiment with lifecycle clearing, uint64 preservation and stable count controls; do not call it a repair without evidence.
privacy: No actual server/player identity values, credentials, tickets, callback CRCs, private endpoints or packet payloads are included.
